messages:
maria: Quick sync — thinking of running an SLA-aware provisioning experiment next week. Goal: reduce reserved GPU cost by 20% while keeping p99 latency < 350ms for hosted customers. Thoughts?

jasper: Love it. Can we clarify constraints: is this at pool-level (dedicated slices) or cluster-level routing?

maria: Pool-level first — dedicated pools can push less warm capacity and use soft-preempt fallback to shared pool. Need safe fallback so production traffic doesn't hit higher tails.

sophia: Two risks: (1) egress quota coupling when we spill to shared pools; (2) noisy neighbor on shared GPUs increasing p99. We can use VLAN shielding + bandwidth tagging to limit egress coupling.

kevin: We have recent telemetry for soft-spill events. Jasper, can you paste the query that shows p99 delta when spill_rate > 5%?

jasper: here's the query I used in the probe dashboard:
```
SELECT pool, percentile(latency, 99) as p99, spill_rate
FROM gpu_requests
WHERE time > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY pool
ORDER BY spill_rate DESC
```
On eu-west shared-slice we saw p99 jump from 280ms -> 540ms when spill_rate ~ 8%.

maria: Oof. That's not acceptable. Proposal: run a canary for 48h with SLA-aware routing that routes up to 4% spill only and then force fallthrough to reserved fallback after thresholds. Also enable KV cache extension for canary tenants.

sophia: Cost model: if we reduce reserved pool by 15% we'll save ~$7.2k/month but expect ~1.2% increase in shared egress usage; estimated additional egress cost ~$1.1k/month. Net savings ~6.1k. Need sign-off.

kevin: +1 on the experiment. We'll need a rollout plan, rollback criteria (p99 > 350ms for > 1% of requests), and communication to enterprise customers.

ops-bot: alert: eu-west shared-slice spike detected — 2023-03-15T08:21:30Z — spill_rate 9.1% — auto-throttle triggered.

jasper: I'll prep the canary config and run 48h in staging first. I'll also instrument a 'spill_tag' in tracing to make debug easier.

maria: Great. @kevin can you do the cost approval? I'll draft the announcement and set on-call playbook.

kevin: Will review today. FYI we should also add a soft cap on concurrent KV cache entries per tenant to avoid cache thrash.
